quotes.text: Release the safety latch and lower yourself slowly by bending your knees until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly lower.

quotes.text: Push back to the starting position by pushing through your heels and extend your knees. Remember to keep your torso upright during the entire movement.

quotes.text: The knees bend and the hips sink into the deep squat position. The torso remains upright the arc of the machine naturally maintains this position. The knees track over the toes throughout.

quotes.text: Descend as deeply as the machine allows and mobility permits the goal is to reach a position where the thighs are at or below parallel to the floor.

quotes.text: Push through the full foot heel and ball driving back up through the pendulum arc to the starting position.

quotes.text: Knees caving inward: Valgus collapse at the knee during the descent or ascent. Fix: actively drive the knees outward in line with the toes throughout. Reduce load if the collapse persists.

quotes.text: Heels rising: Insufficient ankle mobility prevents the heels staying flat through the full depth. Fix: elevate the heels slightly on a plate or wedge while ankle mobility is developed.

quotes.text: Rushing the descent: Dropping into the bottom rather than controlling the lowering phase. Fix: a controlled two to three second descent on every rep.

quotes.text: Primary muscles worked: Quads Glutes Adductors

quotes.text: Primary: Quadriceps all four heads, with particularly significant emphasis on the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis due to the upright torso and deep range of motion.
quotes.closest: Primary: Quadriceps all four heads, with particularly significant emphasis on the rectus femoris and vastus lateralis due to the upright torso and deep range of motion.

quotes.text: Secondary: Gluteus maximus, hamstrings, adductors, gastrocnemius (knee stability).

quotes.text: The pendulum squat is an effective exercise for isolating the quadriceps with minimal pressure on the back. The stabilized movement path of the machine allows for full control throughout, making it a safe and joint-friendly option.

quotes.text: Sets of 8 to 12 repetitions at a challenging load, through full range, are the standard approach for strength and hypertrophy.
